key_findings.detail:
HJT modules experience moisture-dependent, two-level degradation:

- **Level 1 (moisture alone, no voltage bias):** Damp heat (500 hours) causes ~20% Isc loss through water-induced glass corrosion, which produces NaOH molecules that attack the TCO layer even without applied bias
- **Level 2 (negative bias + moisture):** Applied negative voltage accelerates Na⁺ drift through the EVA encapsulant to the TCO layer, creating recombination centers at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface

- [[papers/Wiley-251-3004-2-s2.0-85045834850-2018-J-Comprehensive study of potential-induced degradation in silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell mod.pdf#page=2|Zu et al. (2018), p.2]]

In bifacial HJT modules, the two sides degrade through distinct pathways:

- **Front side (under negative bias):** Isc loss dominates, reaching **53.9% Pmax loss** after 800 h, driven by optical degradation from metallic indium formation in the ITO layer
- **Rear side (different bias polarity):** FF loss dominates, reaching **40.4% Pmax loss** after 800 h
- Positive bias on either face prevents all degradation

- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=3|Luo et al. (2024), p.3]]

Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and TEM analysis reveal:

- **Nano-cracks** form at the ITO surface under PID conditions
- Na⁺ and OH⁻ groups migrate through these nano-cracks into the a-Si:H layers
- Na⁺ creates recombination centers at the a-Si:H/c-Si interface, reducing passivation quality
- Metallic indium (In⁰) is reduced from ITO at sites of Na⁺ accumulation, causing optical absorption losses

- [[papers/Wiley-251-3004-2-s2.0-85045834850-2018-J-Comprehensive study of potential-induced degradation in silicon heterojunction photovoltaic cell mod.pdf#page=3|Zu et al. (2018), p.3]]

Ionomer encapsulant reduces PID in HJT modules dramatically:

- **EVA encapsulant:** 31% Pmax loss after 500 h under PID conditions
- **Ionomer encapsulant:** < 5% Pmax loss after 500 h under the same conditions

This confirms that restricting Na⁺ transport through the encapsulant is the dominant mitigation lever for HJT modules.

- [[papers/Wiley-107-890-2-s2.0-85180462440-2024-J-Potential-induced degradation in bifacial silicon heterojunction solar modules: Insights and mitigat.pdf#page=5|Luo et al. (2024), p.5]]
